svg.aria-label: Polynomial identity theorem and difference polynomial proof
svg.title: Polynomial identity theorem and difference polynomial proof
svg.desc: Four staged panels: agreement at three points, forming the difference polynomial, contradiction with the root bound, and concluding that the difference is the zero polynomial.

g.text: deg(p) ≤ 2 and deg(q) ≤ 2, with agreement at x₁, x₂, x₃.
d has degree at most 2, unless d is the zero polynomial.
A non-zero polynomial of degree ≤ 2 has at most two distinct zeros.
But d has three distinct zeros, so the non-zero case is impossible.
Therefore d(x) ≡ 0, so p(x) = q(x) for every x.
The root bound applies only to non-zero polynomials.
